themes: Gartner (27-Jul-2026): worldwide IT services spend +5.3% in 2026 to US$1,570 bn (ex-IaaS), +3.8% in 2025. NASSCOM (24-Feb-2026): Indian tech revenue +6.1% to ~US$315 bn in FY26, FY27 'similar'. ICRA (27-Feb-2026): Indian IT USD growth 2-3% in FY26, 3-4% in FY27. A low-single-digit market for the largest vendor.
Spend moving to AI infrastructure and software

Gartner: data-centre systems +62.5%, software +15.5%, IaaS +29% in 2026 vs services +5.3%; services fall from 26.8% to 24.7% of IT spend (GAM calculation). BCG IT Spending Pulse (17-Sep-2026): IT budgets +5.8% but the IT-services outlook fell 19 points vs H2-2025, a 'reallocation'. The incremental dollar goes to GPUs, models and software (Kotak, 29-Apr-2026).

TCS: 10-15% productivity gain passed on 'in most places' as contracts renew (Q1FY27 call). HCLTech (Apr-2026): 3-5% deflation in AI-disrupted services, 2-3% for its portfolio; a 'US$100 m deal would be ~US$80 m today'. Kotak base case 3.5% pricing erosion, first in large multi-year renewals. HFS (30-Jun-2026): clients renegotiate within 24 months, not at renewal. ISG (9-Jul-2026): 'pricing deflation and more provider-funded, AI-powered transformation embedded within contracts'.

TCS AI services run-rate US$1.5 bn (Q2FY26) to US$2.6 bn (Q1FY27), ~8.5% of revenue; HCLTech advanced-AI revenue US$171 m, +62% YoY (Q1FY27); Infosys AI 8.2% of revenue (Q1FY27). TCS: AI work earns 'much better' revenue productivity; legacy-modernisation deals of US$5-10 m see no pricing pressure (JM Financial, 8-Sep-2026).

US-Iran war from 28-Feb-2026; Accenture lost ~US$100 m of revenue to the Middle East conflict in its May-2026 quarter; Cognizant cut its 2026 guide to +4.0-5.5% CC as discretionary spend stayed tight (29-Jul-2026); Infosys trimmed FY27 guidance to 1.5-3.0% CC (23-Jul-2026); TCS clients deferred projects in Q1FY27. Brent ~US$97 on 30-Sep-2026.

TCS: six mega deals in five quarters, FY26 TCV US$40.7 bn (FY25 US$39.4 bn); HCLTech record Q1 bookings US$2.41 bn; Cognizant trailing book-to-bill 1.3x; Accenture 104 clients with US$100 m+ bookings in nine months (+13%). But ISG: mega-deal ACV -27% in Q2-2026 and Americas managed services -12%.
Clients in-source work to their own Indian centres; TCS launched a GCC build-operate-transfer business unit (Q1FY27). BCG: net supplier consolidation in every category except AI/ML.
INR/USD from ~85.5 (Q1FY26 average) to 94.8 (Q1FY27) and 95.83 (30-Sep-2026 close, with RBI selling dollars; 5paisa): ~10% more rupees per dollar of revenue, ~110 bp of margin help in Q4FY26 (TCS).

moat: 66 clients over US$100 m and 1,401 over US$1 m a year (Q1FY27); decades-long relationships (e.g. M&S renewed and expanded as a mega deal in Q4FY26); US$40.7 bn of FY26 TCV.
Wins large renewals and consolidation deals; protects share.
FY26 EBITDA margin (Screener basis) 27.1% vs Infosys 23.7%, HCLTech 20.6%, Wipro 19.2%, LTM 17.9%; EBIT 25.0%; best-in-class pyramid and utilisation.
Room to price aggressively and still out-earn peers.
No debt besides leases, ~Rs50,000 cr invested funds, ROE ~50%.
Can fund HyperVault, M&A and payouts at once.
Run contracts are sticky (renewals ~50% of TCV), but AI lowers transition cost and clients renegotiate early.
Mostly people-based services; products (BaNCS, ignio, iON) are small; AI partnerships with Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, Google are not exclusive.
Largest AI book in rupees (US$2.6 bn run-rate) but ~8.5% of revenue and lumpy; growth lagged peers in FY26.
Must show AI is net accretive.

Deal wins do not convert: TCV is high but trailing-twelve-month TCV growth is ~1% and AI additions are slowing
TCS grew 5-6 points slower than its closest peer in FY26, the widest gap on record
Nuvama analyst on the Q4FY26 call
